title: Isomorphism graphs of projective flat curves
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with geometric fibres of dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_T(X\times_ST,Y\times_ST)$, with pullback along morphisms of $S$-schemes [def-pc-fibre-product], is represented by a scheme $J$ separated and of finite presentation over $S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its representing bijection is the graph construction: a $T$-point gives the closed subscheme $\Gamma\subset X_T\times_TY_T$ whose two projections to $X_T$ and $Y_T$ are isomorphisms, and the associated isomorphism is the second projection composed with the inverse of the first. These bijections commute with arbitrary base change. No stability, smoothness, connectedness or marking hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp); scheme realization by projective graphs, using quot.tex Tag 0D01 (proposition-hilb), Tag 0D1B (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb-open), and moduli.tex Tags 0DPN (lemma-Mor-s-lfp), 0DPP (lemma-Isom-in-Mor).

proof.text: Choose projective embeddings and apply the numerical-cover lemma. It gives Noetherian affine opens $U$, proper flat finitely presented restrictions, the Segre embedding of $E=X_U\times_UY_U$, and one coordinate Hilbert polynomial $R$ for all geometric isomorphism graphs.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), numerical quasi-compactness paragraph and displayed graph Euler calculation; perfect.tex Tag 0B9T (lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric); varieties.tex Tag 0AYX (lemma-degree-tensor-product); Segre and coordinate-ring comparison as recorded in the parent steps 1, 2 and 5.

proof.text: Apply the bounded-double-graph lemma to each $E/U$ and $R$. It gives a separated finitely presented $J_U$ representing graphs with both projections invertible. The inverse formula $p_Y\circ p_X^{-1}$ identifies its points with isomorphisms, naturally under every pullback.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), final bounded-open argument; quot.tex Tags 0D1A (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb), 0D1B (lemma-Mor-into-Hilb-open); the projective Hilbert scheme realization and Noetherian permanence in parent steps 3, 4 and 6.

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness, hence separatedness, of both families. Apply the Zariski gluing lemma to the cover and the natural graph representatives $J_U$. It yields the separated finitely presented global representative, both graph formulas, and compatibility with every base change, without imposing Noetherianity on the new base.

source.place: Tag 01JB (lemma-glue), gluing scheme morphisms and inverse identities; Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), open-subfunctor representability; moduli-curves.tex Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), target-local separatedness and finite presentation. This is parent proof steps 7, 8 and 9 with the local graph representatives as hypotheses.
